planningPrinciples: Use one practical hotel base per city; the only intentional return is the final two Seoul nights for a low-stress ICN departure.
Travel by direct KTX on city-change days, with only a light neighborhood plan after check-in.
Group sights by neighborhood rather than crisscrossing each city for a single attraction.
Keep a weather-friendly indoor alternative every day and avoid making time-sensitive events the sole anchor.
Treat all rail times, event dates, pricing, opening hours, and entry rules as details to verify in official apps and sites before purchase.

importantDates.label: CSAT / Suneung day
importantDates.note: Keep this Busan day deliberately low-stakes. Morning traffic management, later office/bank opening, and an approximately 13:05–13:40 aviation hold; verify the current notice before travel.

importantDates.label: 13:00 ICN departure
importantDates.note: Plan to be at the airport around three hours before an international departure, subject to airline guidance. Stay in Seoul the final two nights instead of attempting a same-day Busan-to-ICN connection.

trip.sourceNote: These are deliberately detailed planning blueprints synthesized from the retained transport, hotel, activity, food, savings, and emergency research. They are not confirmations or a live timetable.
trip.scheduleNote: Times below are intentional planning windows, not a live timetable. They are designed to make the day explicit while retaining enough buffer for weather, queues, rests, and transit.
trip.flightReconciliation: The Korea-based plan begins with a local ICN arrival at 21:00 on Nov. 1 and ends with a local ICN departure at 13:00 on Nov. 22. Because Seoul is well ahead of San Francisco, do not assume a Nov. 1 SFO departure can also be a Nov. 1 ICN arrival; reconcile the outbound calendar date, airline, terminal, and arrival time from the actual ticket before booking the first hotel night.
weatherAndPacking: Use layers rather than one heavy coat: a warm mid-layer, wind/rain shell, comfortable broken-in walking shoes, and evening accessories are more useful than a fixed temperature promise.
Check the actual forecast and AirKorea a few days before departure. The route includes outdoor palace, coast, park, and market days, but every one has an indoor or low-walking fallback.
Carry a compact umbrella or waterproof layer, a power bank, a universal Type C/F adapter, any personal medicines in original packaging, and a small day bag for train days.

budgetFrame.label: Stay strategy
budgetFrame.detail: Price live hotel rooms by exact dates and one-bed/private-bath requirements. The plans favor a practical Myeongdong/Seoul Station base, a station-oriented middle-city base, and one Haeundae base rather than costly hotel moves.

budgetFrame.label: Transport strategy
budgetFrame.detail: Direct KTX is the value/convenience default for city changes. T-money/WOWPASS-style local payment remains useful, but re-check current accepted cards, pass coverage, and actual fares.

budgetFrame.label: Experience strategy
budgetFrame.detail: Use a few paid anchors that matter to you, then layer in markets, parks, coastal walks, museums, and neighborhood food. Do not buy a pass solely because it is discounted; compare it with your actual saved list.

budgetFrame.label: Food strategy
budgetFrame.detail: Keep one quality meal or market experience per day, then use convenience-store, bakery, café, or hotel-neighborhood meals to protect pace and budget.

arrivalChecklist: Confirm hotel late check-in and save its Korean address before boarding the last flight.
Keep passport, arrival/entry confirmation, insurance contact, final hotel address, and an offline emergency card accessible before landing.
Choose the airport transfer based on live arrival time, luggage, terminal, and hotel—not a generic cheapest-fare rule.
Do not schedule sightseeing, a nonrefundable dinner, or a timed ticket on the arrival night.
departureChecklist: Complete online check-in and verify the airline terminal, baggage allowance, and airport cutoff the day before.
Pack passports, cards, devices, receipts/tax-refund paperwork, and medicines in a known carry-on location on Nov. 21.
Leave central Seoul early enough to be at ICN around three hours before the 13:00 international departure, following airline advice.
Handle airline, security, and any valid tax-refund process before duty-free browsing or a meal.
trip.budgetMethodNote: Hotel examples below multiply the retained research's indicative one-room nightly USD ranges by the planned nights. They are planning math only: taxes, service fees, room type, weekend/date demand, currency conversion, promotions, and availability can materially change the real total.
dailySpendGuardrails: Keep food, local transit, and paid activities as separate envelopes rather than relying on the rough draft's old all-in daily price. Your actual balance depends on how many paid anchors you keep.
Use the planner's saved ideas and route days to identify the handful of paid tickets, reservations, spa/cooking-class choices, and special meals that deserve a confirmed budget.
Price the full transportation stack only after the airline, KTX trains, airport transfer, local payment card/pass, and hotel districts are selected.
flightBookingChecklist: Search to the actual local ICN arrival target first: 21:00 on Nov. 1. The originating SFO calendar date may be earlier because Seoul is far ahead of San Francisco.

Compare live direct and one-stop options by total arrival time, baggage/cancellation terms, seat comfort, airline terminal, and the ability to reach the Seoul hotel after immigration—not by an old fare screenshot.
After purchase, add flight numbers, both airport terminals, airline check-in cutoff, baggage allowance, seat assignment, and travel-insurance details to My plan.
Do not build a nonrefundable Seoul arrival-night plan until the flight and the hotel's late check-in policy are confirmed.

itineraries.title: Capital, Science Hub & Coastal Panoramas (Classic Explorer)
itineraries.bestFor: First-time travelers seeking a balanced, comprehensive introduction to Korea's imperial palaces, cutting-edge science and bakery culture in Daejeon, and dynamic coastal Busan highlights.
itineraries.decisionSummary: The quintessential three-city route balancing royal history, high-tech research hubs, and marine scenery with beginner-friendly pacing.
itineraries.recommendation: Choose this route if you want the classic South Korea experience with a smooth, structured pace and rich regional variety.
itineraries.tradeoff: Daejeon requires a bit more transit time between attractions than Cheonan, and you cover substantial walking daily across three distinct major cities.

bases.why: Central subway interchange (Line 1/4/2 access), direct AREX connection, easy walking to Deoksugung, Namdaemun, and Myeongdong, and minimal friction for the Sunday morning KTX departure.
hotelIdeas: Four Points by Sheraton Josun Seoul Station
Nine Tree Premier Hotel Myeongdong II

bases.why: Direct subway connection (Line 1) to Daejeon KTX Station, natural mineral hot spring foot baths on the street, and close proximity to KAIST, Expo Science Park, and Hanbat Arboretum.
hotelIdeas: Yuseong Hotel / Ramada by Wyndham Daejeon

bases.why: Walk to Haeundae Beach, Blueline Park coastal train, Centum City Spa Land, and direct bus/metro connections across the eastern and southern coast.
Guarantees a stress-free AREX Non-Stop express connection to Incheon Airport on Sunday morning and eliminates all risk of high-speed rail disruption on flight day.
hotelIdeas: Four Points by Sheraton Josun Seoul Station
Nine Tree Premier Hotel Myeongdong II

transfers.recommended: Airport Limousine Bus (e.g. 6001/6015) or AREX All-Stop/Express depending on terminal and hotel location; Official Airport Taxi queue if arriving with heavy luggage after 21:00.
transfers.why: Late arrival at 21:00 means clearing customs around 22:15. Direct bus or taxi drops luggage at hotel doorstep without late-night subway transfers.

transfers.recommended: KTX High-Speed Rail (approx. 50–60 minutes, direct).
transfers.why: Frequent 15–20 minute departure intervals; smooth transition from central Seoul to central Daejeon with minimal transit fatigue.

transfers.recommended: KTX High-Speed Rail (approx. 1 hour 30 minutes, direct).
transfers.why: Fastest and most comfortable connection from central Daejeon to coastal Busan, arriving in time for check-in and sunset seafood dinner.

transfers.recommended: KTX High-Speed Rail (approx. 2 hours 15 minutes, direct).
transfers.why: Returning to Seoul 2 nights before international flight buffers against rail weather delays and allows relaxed final souvenir shopping.

transfers.recommended: AREX Non-Stop Express Train (43 min to T1, 51 min to T2) with Seoul Station City Airport Terminal check-in if eligible.
transfers.why: Punctual, climate-controlled, dedicated luggage racks, arriving 3 hours before the 13:00 flight.

budgetScenarios.label: Value Comfort (3-Star Boutique & Business Stays)
budgetScenarios.assumptions: Double room with private bath; Nine Tree Myeongdong, Ramada Daejeon, Felix by STX Haeundae.
budgetScenarios.note: Excellent cleanliness, prime station/metro proximity, laundry facilities, high walking score.

budgetScenarios.label: Upscale Premium (4 to 5-Star City & Ocean View Stays)
budgetScenarios.assumptions: King room with breakfast; L7 Myeongdong, Hotel Onoma Daejeon, Signiel or Grand Josun Busan.
budgetScenarios.note: Panoramic skyline views, thermal spa access, luxury bedding, premier fitness amenities.

bookingPriorities: Reconcile SFO outbound flight with Nov 1 21:00 local ICN arrival and Nov 22 13:00 departure.
Reserve 4 hotel base stays with free cancellation (Seoul 7N, Daejeon 5N, Busan 7N, Seoul 2N).
Book 3 KTX rail legs on Korail app 30 days prior to travel (Seoul→Daejeon, Daejeon→Busan, Busan→Seoul).
Reserve AREX Non-Stop Airport Express tickets and pre-order Korea eSIM / T-Money / WOWPASS card.
Secure timed reservations for special experiences (e.g. Changdeokgung Secret Garden, Spa Land, fine dining).

days.title: Land softly; do not turn arrival night into sightseeing
days.anchor: ICN arrival at 21:00 → late transfer → hotel check-in → sleep

schedule.title: ICN Arrival & Border Clearance
schedule.detail: Clear immigration, collect checked luggage, and pick up pre-booked eSIM / T-Money transport card at terminal arrivals hall.
schedule.logistics: Terminal 1 or 2 depending on flight carrier.

schedule.title: Airport Transfer to Central Seoul
schedule.detail: Board Airport Limousine Bus (6001/6015) or official airport taxi queue directly to hotel in Myeongdong / Seoul Station.
schedule.logistics: Direct drop-off minimizes late-night stair transfers with heavy bags.

schedule.title: Hotel Check-in & Rest
schedule.detail: Check into hotel room, unpack essentials, grab warm water or tea, and get restorative sleep.
schedule.logistics: Notify hotel front desk of late check-in in advance.

blocks.label: Arrival Protocol
blocks.text: Preserve physical energy after international transit; do not schedule dining reservations.

blocks.label: Direct Transport
blocks.text: Airport bus or taxi eliminates confusing subway line transfers at midnight.

days.food: Light convenience store snack (CU / GS25 warm samgak kimbap or banana milk) or room service.
days.reservationNote: Confirm late check-in with hotel in writing 48 hours prior.
days.costNote: Airport Limousine bus ~₩17,000 / Deluxe Taxi ~₩85,000.
days.watchouts: Late night jetlag; keep bedtime calm without heavy alcohol.
days.planB: If flight is delayed past 23:00, use official International Taxi counter at ICN Hall 4C/8C.

days.title: Imperial Grandeur & Traditional Hanok Quarters
days.anchor: Gyeongbokgung Palace Guard Changing → Bukchon Hanok Village → Insadong Tea Alley

schedule.title: Gyeongbokgung Royal Palace
schedule.detail: Witness the vibrant Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at Gwanghwamun Gate (10:00 AM) and explore the majestic Geunjeongjeon throne hall and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion.
schedule.logistics: Subway Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung Station Exit 5.

schedule.title: Samcheong-dong Traditional Lunch
schedule.detail: Stroll leafy Samcheong-dong street and savor handmade sujebi (potato-dough pasta soup) or bulgogi.
schedule.logistics: 10-minute gentle walk from palace east gate.

schedule.title: Bukchon Hanok Village Walk
schedule.detail: Wander preserved Joseon-era residential alleys with traditional tiled roofs overlooking modern Seoul skyline.
schedule.logistics: Uphill stone pathways; please respect quiet residential zone rules.

schedule.title: Insadong Antique Street & Ssamzigil
schedule.detail: Browse calligraphy shops, artisan crafts, and sip roasted traditional jujube or omija tea in a wooden hanok teahouse.

schedule.title: Welcome Korean BBQ Dinner
schedule.detail: Enjoy aged pork belly (samgyeopsal) grilled over charcoal with fresh ssam lettuce wraps and doenjang stew.

blocks.label: Clustered Geography
blocks.text: Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon, and Insadong are contiguous northern heritage districts, requiring zero subway hops during the day.

blocks.label: Autumn Ambience
blocks.text: Early November offers golden ginkgo foliage along Samcheong-dong and palace walls.

days.food: Lunch: Samcheong-dong Sujebi (Michelin Bib Gourmand). Dinner: Jongno charcoal-grilled pork belly with soybean stew.
days.reservationNote: Palace closed on Tuesdays; entry ₩3,000 (free if wearing hanbok).
days.costNote: Sightseeing entry ₩3,000; meals ~₩35,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Bukchon is a quiet residential area; quiet hours strictly enforced after 17:00.
days.planB: National Folk Museum of Korea located inside palace grounds if weather turns rainy.

days.title: Secret Royal Landscapes & Street Food Feasts
days.anchor: Changdeokgung Huwon Secret Garden → Ikseon-dong Hanok Cafes → Gwangjang Market

schedule.title: Changdeokgung Palace & Secret Garden (Huwon)
schedule.detail: Explore UNESCO World Heritage Changdeokgung and take a guided walking tour through the serene autumn Secret Garden pavilions and lotus ponds.

schedule.title: Ikseon-dong Hanok Alleys & Lunch
schedule.detail: Discover retro-modern hanok alleys filled with artisanal bakeries, fusion cafes, and craft boutiques.

schedule.title: Jongmyo Royal Ancestral Shrine & Cheonggyecheon
schedule.detail: Walk the solemn grounds of Jongmyo Shrine and follow the tranquil Cheonggyecheon Stream pedestrian walkway.

schedule.title: Gwangjang Traditional Food Market
schedule.detail: Experience Korea's oldest market feast: crispy mung bean pancakes (bindaetteok), mayak gimbap, and beef tartare (yukhoe).

blocks.label: Secret Garden Timing
blocks.text: Huwon requires advance timed reservation; early November autumn foliage here is world-famous.

blocks.label: Seamless Walkway
blocks.text: Connecting Changdeokgung through Ikseon-dong to Gwangjang Market is a straight, flat pedestrian route.

days.food: Lunch: Ikseon-dong hanok cafe (steamed egg toast or kalguksu). Dinner: Gwangjang Market bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and makgeolli.
days.reservationNote: Book Changdeokgung Huwon Secret Garden ticket online 6 days in advance at 10:00 AM KST.
days.costNote: Palace + Garden entry ₩8,000; Market food ~₩20,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Gwangjang market food stalls are cash/T-money preferred; evening crowds can be dense.
days.planB: If heavy rain occurs, explore underground Jongno arcades and Gwangjang covered market.

days.title: Masterpiece Artifacts & Mountain Skyline Views
days.anchor: National Museum of Korea → Yongsan Family Park → N Seoul Tower Sunset

schedule.title: National Museum of Korea
schedule.detail: Marvel at Korean national treasures including the Pensive Bodhisattva statues in the Room of Quiet Contemplation and Ten-Story Gyeongcheonsa Pagoda.
schedule.logistics: Ichon Station Line 4 / Gyeongui-Jungang Line direct underground connection.

schedule.title: Ichon-dong Japanese Dining / Fusion Lunch
schedule.detail: Enjoy lunch in Little Tokyo Ichon-dong or museum garden lakeside restaurant.

schedule.title: War Memorial of Korea
schedule.detail: Tour the expansive outdoor aircraft and naval exhibitions and solemn indoor memorial halls.

schedule.title: N Seoul Tower & Namsan Sunset
schedule.detail: Ascend Namsan via scenic cable car or shuttle bus to enjoy 360-degree sunset views over the entire Seoul metropolitan basin.
schedule.logistics: Myeongdong Namsan Cable Car or Yellow Shuttle Bus #01.

schedule.title: Myeongdong Kyoja Dumpling Dinner
schedule.detail: Savor Michelin Bib Gourmand handmade pork dumplings (mandu) and rich chicken broth kalguksu with spicy garlic kimchi.

blocks.label: Cultural Depth
blocks.text: National Museum provides essential historical context before traveling to regional Joseon and Silla cities.

blocks.label: Sunset Alignment
blocks.text: Reaching N Seoul Tower by 16:30 captures day, golden hour, and shimmering city nightscape in one visit.

days.food: Lunch: Ichon Japanese katsu / Udon or Museum Garden Cafe. Dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja (handmade kalguksu and steamed mandu).
days.reservationNote: National Museum permanent galleries are free; special exhibitions may require ticket.
days.costNote: N Seoul Tower observatory ₩21,000; Cable car round-trip ₩15,000.
days.watchouts: Cable car queue can be 30–45 mins on clear evenings; shuttle bus 01 is faster alternative.
days.planB: National Museum of Korea is fully climate-controlled with vast indoor galleries.

days.title: Creative Hubs, Urban Greenways & Coffee Culture
days.anchor: Hongdae Indie Culture → Gyeongui Line Forest Park → Yeonnam-dong Boutique Cafes

schedule.title: Gyeongui Line Forest Park Stroll
schedule.detail: Walk the transformed former railway corridor lined with boutique shops, craft bakeries, and autumn trees.
schedule.logistics: Hongik Univ. Station Line 2 / AREX Exit 3.

schedule.title: Yeonnam-dong Trendy Dining Lunch
schedule.detail: Enjoy artisanal handmade pasta, Korean rice bowls, or fresh bakery treats in trendy Yeonnam-dong.

schedule.title: Hongdae Shopping & Indie Arts Street
schedule.detail: Browse unique Korean streetwear, stationary shops (Object, KT&G Sangsangmadang), and photo studios.

schedule.title: Hongdae Live Street Busking
schedule.detail: Watch talented young K-pop dancers, acoustic musicians, and indie performers on Hongdae busking street.

schedule.title: Mapo Charcoal Galbi Barbecue Feast
schedule.detail: Feast on marinated pork ribs grilled over charcoal accompanied by refreshing cold dongchimi broth.

blocks.label: Youth Energy
blocks.text: Hongdae comes alive in the afternoon and evening with creative youth culture and music.

blocks.label: Walkable Greenway
blocks.text: Forest park provides a calming pedestrian buffer between bustling commercial streets.

days.food: Lunch: Yeonnam-dong Korean fusion bibimbap or handmade burger. Dinner: Mapo Original Galbi pork ribs.
days.reservationNote: Most retail and indie shops in Hongdae open around 11:00 AM.
days.costNote: Budget ~₩40,000 per person for dining and dessert cafes.
days.watchouts: Evening crowds in Hongdae on Friday/weekend get dense; keep valuables secure.
days.planB: KT&G Sangsangmadang offers multi-floor indoor art gallery, cinema, and design shop.

days.title: Cutting-Edge Design & Brooklyn of Seoul
days.anchor: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) → Seongsu-dong Concept Lofts → Han River Sunset Cruise

schedule.title: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
schedule.detail: Explore Zaha Hadid's futuristic architectural masterpiece, design museums, innovation showrooms, and rooftop gardens.
schedule.logistics: Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station Line 2/4/5 Exit 1.

schedule.title: Seongsu-dong Industrial Loft Lunch
schedule.detail: Experience transformed red-brick shoe factory cafes and dining spaces in trendy Seongsu-dong.

schedule.title: Seongsu Flagship Boutiques (Tamburins, Gentle Monster, Daelim)
schedule.detail: Visit experiential architecture and multi-sensory concept stores across Seongsu Yeonmujang-gil.

schedule.title: Ttukseom Hangang Park & Sunset View
schedule.detail: Relax along the Han River bank, enjoy automated Han River convenience store instant ramen, and watch the sunset.

schedule.title: Sindang-dong Tteokbokki Town Supper
schedule.detail: Enjoy famous bubbling tabletop spicy rice cakes cooked with ramen, dumplings, fishcakes, and eggs.

blocks.label: Modern Contrasts
blocks.text: Balances Seoul's futuristic architecture with industrial revitalization in Seongsu.

blocks.label: Riverside Relaxation
blocks.text: Hangang park break prevents city fatigue and showcases everyday local Seoul life.

days.food: Lunch: Seongsu Daelim Warehouse cafe dining. Dinner: Sindang-dong Tteokbokki Town shared boiling pot.
days.reservationNote: DDP design store opens at 10:00; architecture exterior accessible 24/7.
days.costNote: DDP exhibits ~₩15,000; Tteokbokki dinner ~₩12,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Seongsu popular flagship stores may have short digital queue wait times on weekends.
days.planB: DDP indoor design labs and Seongsu Daelim Warehouse provide covered indoor shelter.

days.title: Glamour, Grand Libraries & Ancient Urban Sanctuary
days.anchor: Starfield COEX Library → Bongeunsa Millennium Temple → Han River Park Walk

schedule.title: Starfield COEX Library & Mega Mall
schedule.detail: Photograph the magnificent 13-meter tall book towers at Starfield Library and browse Asian largest underground shopping complex.
schedule.logistics: Samseong Station Line 2 Exit 6 or Bongeunsa Station Line 9 Exit 7.

schedule.title: Parnas Mall Gourmet Lunch
schedule.detail: Enjoy Korean modern beef soup (gomtang) or royal hot pot in the lower level gourmet arcade.

schedule.title: Bongeunsa Buddhist Temple
schedule.detail: Step across the street into an ancient peaceful temple founded in 794 AD, home to a majestic 23-meter stone Maitreya Buddha.

schedule.title: Apgujeong Rodeo & K-Star Road
schedule.detail: Walk Gangnam upscale fashion district, K-Star Road art bear statues, and Dosan Park cafes.
schedule.logistics: Apgujeong Rodeo Station Suin-Bundang Line Exit 2.

schedule.title: Seoul Station Prep & Early Sleep
schedule.detail: Return to Myeongdong / Seoul Station base, pack primary luggage for Sunday KTX transit, and enjoy dinner.
schedule.logistics: Subway Line 4 return to Seoul Station.

blocks.label: Temple & Tower Harmony
blocks.text: Bongeunsa's serene incense and ancient wood sits in mesmerizing contrast to Gangnam glass skyscrapers.

blocks.label: Transit Prep
blocks.text: Finishing early on Saturday night guarantees relaxed packing before Sunday morning KTX to Daejeon.

days.food: Lunch: Hadongkwan 80-year Gomtang beef soup at COEX. Dinner: Myeongdong Dakgalbi spicy stir-fried chicken.
days.reservationNote: Bongeunsa Temple is free entry; open until 22:00.
days.costNote: Free entry to COEX library and temple; meals ~₩30,000 per person.
days.watchouts: COEX underground mall is vast; follow overhead color-coded floor navigation lines.
days.planB: COEX mall and Aquarium provide 100% weather-proof indoor environment.

days.title: High-Speed Rail into Korea's Science & Bakery Capital
days.anchor: Morning KTX Seoul to Daejeon (55 mins) → Sung Sim Dang Main Bakery → Expo Hanbit Tower Sunset

schedule.title: Seoul Station Departure
schedule.detail: Walk to Seoul Station from hotel, grab morning coffee, and board direct KTX high-speed train.
schedule.logistics: Board train 10 minutes before departure; assigned carriage and seats.

schedule.title: KTX to Daejeon Station
schedule.detail: Smooth 55-minute high-speed transit through central South Korea plains.
schedule.logistics: Daejeon Station is a major hub on Gyeongbu Line.

schedule.title: Sung Sim Dang Legendary Bakery & Eunhaeng-dong
schedule.detail: Visit Korea's most celebrated historic bakery (since 1956) for warm Twigim Soboro (fried streusel pastry) and Panna Cotta; stroll Jungang Market.

schedule.title: Hotel Check-in & Settle in Yuseong / Dunsan
schedule.detail: Check into Daejeon base hotel (e.g. Hotel Onoma or Ramada Yuseong) and refresh.
schedule.logistics: Daejeon Metro Line 1 or short taxi.

schedule.title: Expo Science Park & Hanbit Tower Media Facade
schedule.detail: Visit the 1993 Daejeon Expo site, ascend Hanbit Tower observatory for sunset, and witness Expo Bridge light reflections.

schedule.title: Daejeon Spicy Dubu Duruchigi Dinner
schedule.detail: Savor Daejeon authentic specialty: spicy braised tofu stir-fry with knife-cut noodles (kalguksu sari).
schedule.logistics: Famous local spots in Daeheung-dong or Dunsan-dong.

blocks.label: Mid-Morning Transit
blocks.text: Leaving Seoul at 10:30 allows a relaxed breakfast without rush-hour luggage congestion.

blocks.label: Bakery Legend
blocks.text: Visiting Sung Sim Dang on arrival day introduces Daejeon beloved food icon.

days.food: Lunch: Sung Sim Dang fresh bakery delights & Jungang Market street snacks. Dinner: Gwangcheon Sikdang spicy Dubu Duruchigi tofu.
days.reservationNote: Book KTX Seoul→Daejeon on Korail app 30 days prior.
days.costNote: KTX ticket ~₩23,700 per person.
days.watchouts: Sung Sim Dang can have lines, but queues move swiftly (under 15 mins).
days.planB: Daejeon Shinsegae Art & Science offers multi-level indoor complex and observatory if rainy.

days.title: Pioneering Science, Robotics & Thermal Spring Relief
days.anchor: National Science Museum → KAIST Campus → Yuseong Outdoor Hot Spring Foot Bath

schedule.title: National Science Museum & Science Center
schedule.detail: Tour Korea's foremost science museum featuring the Hall of Science & Technology, Natural History, and dynamic interactive physics pavilions.
schedule.logistics: Yuseong-gu Daedeok Science Town; City Bus 104/121.

schedule.title: Daedeok Innopolis Research Valley Lunch
schedule.detail: Enjoy lunch at university faculty dining or local dolsot bibimbap restaurant.

schedule.title: KAIST Campus & Innovation Walk
schedule.detail: Explore the peaceful grounds of Korea's premier science institute (duck pond, high-tech labs, and student innovation center).

schedule.title: Yuseong Hot Springs Outdoor Foot Bath Park
schedule.detail: Dip tired feet into 100% natural 42°C alkaline mineral thermal waters in the landscaped public outdoor hot spring park.
schedule.logistics: Yuseong Spa Station Line 1 Exit 7; free public facility, bring a small towel.

schedule.title: Yuseong Traditional Duck Stew (Oritang) Dinner
schedule.detail: Warm up with a hearty clay pot of simmered duck with wild perilla seeds and seasonal greens.

blocks.label: Science & Relaxation
blocks.text: Pairs intellectual discovery at KAIST with therapeutic thermal foot bathing in Yuseong.

blocks.label: Neighborhood Flow
blocks.text: All sites are clustered inside western Daejeon / Yuseong-gu, eliminating cross-city commutes.

days.food: Lunch: KAIST student boulevard stone-pot bibimbap. Dinner: Yuseong mineral water duck stew or Hanwoo beef bulgogi.
days.reservationNote: National Science Museum Hall of Science is free; planetarium requires small fee (₩2,000).
days.costNote: Museum free; Foot bath free; Dinner ~₩25,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Bring a hand towel for drying feet after Yuseong outdoor foot bath.
days.planB: National Science Museum is completely indoor and vast.

days.title: Urban Botanical Oases & Modern Fine Art
days.anchor: Hanbat Arboretum Autumn Metasequoia → Lee Ungno Museum → Dunsan Dining Quarter

schedule.title: Hanbat Arboretum (West & East Gardens)
schedule.detail: Walk through Korea's largest artificial urban arboretum, featuring golden metasequoia walkways, pine forests, and wetland lotus ponds.
schedule.logistics: Govt Complex Daejeon Station Line 1 or City Bus 604/911.

schedule.title: Dunsan Cafe Boulevard Lunch
schedule.detail: Enjoy lunch near Dunsan government center (hand-rolled mandu or tonkatsu).

schedule.title: Lee Ungno Museum of Art & Daejeon Museum of Art
schedule.detail: Admire the modernist white stone architecture by Laurent Beaudouin and explore the abstract calligraphy paintings of master artist Lee Ungno.
schedule.logistics: Located inside Expo park cultural grounds.

schedule.title: Daejeon Shinsegae Art & Science Sky Park
schedule.detail: Take the high-speed elevator to the 38th floor Starbucks and rooftop sculpture terrace overlooking the Gapcheon River.

schedule.title: Daejeon Kalguksu & Suyuk Dinner
schedule.detail: Feast on rich clam-broth hand-cut noodles and tender steamed pork belly slices (suyuk).

blocks.label: Aesthetic Balance
blocks.text: Combines natural autumn landscape with world-class fine art and panoramic city river views.

blocks.label: Central Positioning
blocks.text: All destinations surround the Gapcheon River cultural corridor.

days.food: Lunch: Dunsan handmade dumpling soup. Dinner: Famous Daejeon hand-cut clam kalguksu with suyuk boiled pork.
days.reservationNote: Lee Ungno Museum closed on Mondays; entry ₩1,000.
days.costNote: Hanbat Arboretum is free; Museum entry ₩1,000; Shinsegae sky lounge free.
days.watchouts: Dress warmly for rooftop sky garden terrace in November breezes.
days.planB: Daejeon Museum of Art and Shinsegae Art Center are fully indoor.

days.title: Healing Earth Trails & Scholar Heritage
days.anchor: Gyejoksan Mountain Barefoot Red Clay Trail → Dongchundang Historic Hanok

schedule.title: Gyejoksan Red Clay Trail Walk
schedule.detail: Experience Korea's famous 14.5km natural red clay mountain trail (earthing therapy) through crisp autumn pine forests up to Gyejoksanseong Stone Fortress.
schedule.logistics: City Bus 74 from Daejeon Station or 25-minute taxi to Jangdong forest entrance.

schedule.title: Jangdong Local Farmer Lunch
schedule.detail: Enjoy country-style acorn jelly salad (dotorimuk), potato pancakes (gamjajeon), and fresh wild greens bibimbap.
schedule.logistics: Base village restaurants at trail entrance.

schedule.title: Dongchundang Historic House (Joseon Scholar Residence)
schedule.detail: Tour the 17th-century wooden estate and serene scholar pavilion of Song Jun-gil, showcasing Joseon aristocratic architecture.

schedule.title: Yuseong Thermal Spa Mineral Bath Reset
schedule.detail: Soak in a traditional indoor mineral hot spring bathhouse to relax leg muscles after mountain hiking.

schedule.title: Grilled Eel (Jangeo-gui) Feast
schedule.detail: Replenish stamina with charcoal-grilled freshwater eel seasoned with sweet ginger soy glaze.

blocks.label: Earthing & Wellness
blocks.text: Gyejoksan's soft clay trail is a signature Daejeon natural wellness experience.

blocks.label: Thermal Recovery
blocks.text: Ending the hiking day with a Yuseong hot spring soak completely relieves physical fatigue.

days.food: Lunch: Jangdong forest village dotorimuk and potato pancake. Dinner: Yuseong charcoal-grilled freshwater eel with seasoned rice.
days.reservationNote: Wash stations with clean water are available along Gyejoksan clay trail.
days.costNote: Trail and Dongchundang are free; Thermal bath ~₩10,000; Dinner ~₩35,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Wear comfortable walking shoes with socks easy to remove if walking barefoot on red clay.
days.planB: If rainy, replace hiking with the Daejeon Modern History Museum and indoor spa day.

days.title: Soaring Metasequoia Canopies & Serene Lakeside Panoramas
days.anchor: Jangtaesan Metasequoia Forest Canopy Skywalk → Daecheongho Lake Eco Walk

schedule.title: Jangtaesan Recreational Metasequoia Forest
schedule.detail: Walk among towering 30-meter autumn metasequoia trees, traverse the elevated canopy skywalk bridge, and climb the wooden sky tower.
schedule.logistics: City Bus 20 or 35-minute taxi to Jangan-dong.

schedule.title: Lakeside Country Duck Stew Lunch
schedule.detail: Enjoy country chicken stew (dakbokkeumtang) or grilled mountain mushrooms at a rustic lakeside cottage.

schedule.title: Daecheongho Lake Waterfront Eco Trail
schedule.detail: Stroll the wooden boardwalks around vast Daecheongho Lake, capturing shimmering water reflections and autumn reed fields.

schedule.title: Sung Sim Dang DCC Branch & Farewell Daejeon Stroll
schedule.detail: Pick up fresh baked goods for tomorrow train ride at the DCC branch and walk the Gapcheon riverside promenade.

schedule.title: Daejeon Galbi BBQ Dinner
schedule.detail: Enjoy sweet soy-marinated pork galbi grilled over real wood charcoal.

blocks.label: Spectacular Autumn Foliage
blocks.text: Jangtaesan's metasequoias reach peak rust-orange coloring in early-to-mid November.

blocks.label: Daejeon Completion
blocks.text: Concludes 5 memorable nights in Daejeon with pristine forest and lake scenery.

days.food: Lunch: Jangtaesan rustic spicy chicken stew (dakbokkeumtang). Dinner: Dunsan charcoal pork galbi with cold noodles.
days.reservationNote: Jangtaesan skywalk open 09:00–17:00; admission is free.
days.costNote: Free park entry; Taxi transfers ~₩25,000 each way; Dinner ~₩28,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Canopy suspension bridge can sway gently in high winds; hold railings.
days.planB: Daecheong Dam Water Culture Center and indoor cafes provide covered lake viewing.

days.title: Coastward Bound: High-Speed Rail to the Maritime Capital
days.anchor: Morning KTX Daejeon to Busan (1h30m) → Haeundae Beach Hotel Check-in → Sunset Beach Walk

schedule.title: KTX High-Speed Rail to Busan

schedule.logistics: Arrive at Busan Station central concourse.

schedule.title: Busan Station Choryang Milmyeon Lunch
schedule.detail: Step outside Busan Station to savor famous cold wheat noodles (milmyeon) and steamed king dumplings.
schedule.logistics: Choryang-dong dining street directly opposite station.

schedule.title: Metro / Taxi to Haeundae Beachfront
schedule.detail: Travel to Haeundae hotel base (Metro Line 2 to Haeundae Station or 35-min taxi along Busan Harbor Bridge).
schedule.logistics: Check into hotel (e.g. L7 Haeundae or Felix by STX).

schedule.title: Haeundae Beach Promenade & Dongbaekseok Island Walk
schedule.detail: Stroll white sands of Haeundae Beach and follow the wooden coastal boardwalk around pine-scented Dongbaek Island to APEC Nurimaru House.

schedule.title: Haeundae Traditional Market Seafood Dinner
schedule.detail: Walk Haeundae market street and feast on grilled sea eel (godeulbaegi), fresh seafood hot pot, and famous seed hotteok (ssiat hotteok).

blocks.label: Painless Transit
blocks.text: Direct 90-minute KTX arrives in Busan by noon, leaving the full afternoon for coastal air and beach walking.

blocks.label: Haeundae Anchor
blocks.text: Staying in Haeundae provides seven nights of oceanfront serenity without changing hotels.

days.food: Lunch: Choryang Milmyeon (Busan wheat cold noodles & giant dumplings). Dinner: Haeundae Traditional Market grilled seafood hot pot & ssiat hotteok.

days.watchouts: Dongbaek Island trail is paved and lighted; Nurimaru APEC House closes at 17:00.

days.title: Ocean Rails, Sky Capsules & Coastal Cliff Sanctuaries
days.anchor: Haeundae Blueline Park Beach Train to Cheongsapo → Haedong Yonggungsa Seaside Temple

schedule.detail: Ride a private colorful Sky Capsule cabin 10 meters above the sea along picturesque coastal cliffs to Cheongsapo fishing village.
schedule.logistics: Mipo Station; book tickets 2 weeks in advance online.

schedule.title: Cheongsapo Twin Lighthouses & Grilled Clam Lunch
schedule.detail: Photograph the red and white twin lighthouses, walk the Daritdol Ocean Skywalk, and enjoy fresh grilled clams (jogae-gui).

schedule.title: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple (Temple by the Sea)
schedule.detail: Visit Korea's most dramatic Buddhist temple built directly onto coastal granite rocks, listening to crashing waves below.

schedule.title: Ananti Cove & Coastal Promenade Stroll
schedule.detail: Explore the luxury coastal promenade, oceanfront bookstore (Eternal Journey), and seaside cafe terrace in Gijang.

schedule.title: Gwangalli Beach & Saturday Drone Light Show
schedule.detail: Watch 500+ synchronized LED drones dance over Gwangan Diamond Suspension Bridge from the sandy beachfront.
schedule.logistics: Gwangalli Beach; Saturday shows at 19:00 & 21:00 (winter schedule).

blocks.label: Eastern Coastal Synergy
blocks.text: Blueline Park, Cheongsapo, Yonggungsa, and Gwangalli form a natural eastern coastline day.

blocks.label: Saturday Drone Spectacular
blocks.text: Timed specifically for Saturday evening to witness Gwangalli's world-renowned drone performance.

days.food: Lunch: Cheongsapo seaside grilled clams (jogae-gui) with butter and cheese. Dinner: Gwangalli beachfront raw fish / Korean craft beer and fried chicken.
days.reservationNote: Book Blueline Park Sky Capsule 14 days in advance on official website (sells out fast).
days.costNote: Sky Capsule 2-person cabin ₩35,000; Yonggungsa Temple is free entry.
days.watchouts: Haedong Yonggungsa has stone steps down to the cliffs; wear non-slip shoes.
days.planB: Eternal Journey Bookstore at Ananti and Centum City provide covered coastal alternatives.

days.title: Pastel Hillside Alleys & Korea's Largest Marine Market
days.anchor: Gamcheon Culture Village → Jagalchi Fish Market → Nampo-dong & BIFF Square

schedule.title: Gamcheon Culture Village Walk
schedule.detail: Wander terraced hillside alleys painted in pastel hues, find quirky art installations, and photograph the famous Little Prince and Desert Fox statue overlooking the sea.
schedule.logistics: Toseong Station Line 1 Exit 6, then Local Bus Saha 1-1 or taxi up hill.

schedule.title: Jagalchi Fish Market Feast
schedule.detail: Explore Korea's biggest seafood market; select fresh seasonal sashimi, snow crab, or grilled fish and dine in the second-floor market hall.

schedule.title: BIFF Square & Bupyeong Kkangtong Market
schedule.detail: Walk the Busan International Film Festival handprint square, taste famous seed hotteok, and browse traditional retro market alleys.

schedule.title: Yongdusan Park & Busan Tower Night View
schedule.detail: Ride the outdoor covered escalator up to Yongdusan Park to view twinkling harbor lights from Busan Diamond Tower.

schedule.title: Nampo-dong Dwaeji Gukbap Dinner
schedule.detail: Enjoy boiling pork bone soup with tender pork slices, chives, salted shrimp, and rice.

blocks.label: Old Busan Heritage
blocks.text: Reveals the resilient history of wartime refugees in Gamcheon and the vibrant maritime spirit of Jagalchi.

blocks.label: Food Immersion
blocks.text: Tasting Jagalchi fresh fish and BIFF street snacks is essential Busan culinary culture.

days.food: Lunch: Jagalchi Market 2F fresh flounder sashimi & spicy maeuntang fish soup. Dinner: Traditional Busan Dwaeji Gukbap (rich pork soup).
days.reservationNote: Gamcheon village maps available at tourist center for ₩2,000 (includes stamp rally).
days.costNote: Gamcheon entry free; Busan Tower observation deck ₩12,000.

days.planB: Jagalchi 7-story indoor market building and Nampo Lotte Department store offer full indoor comfort.

days.title: Dramatic Coastal Headlands & Over-Water Gondolas
days.anchor: Taejongdae Ocean Cliff Park → Songdo Marine Cable Car & Skywalk

schedule.title: Taejongdae Resort Park & Danubi Train
schedule.detail: Ride the Danubi park train through dense evergreen forests out to Yeongdo lighthouse and sheer sea cliffs overlooking the Korea Strait.
schedule.logistics: Bus 88/101 from Busan Station or 30-min taxi from hotel.

schedule.title: Yeongdo Coastal Seafood Lunch
schedule.detail: Enjoy fresh sea squirt bibimbap, abalone porridge, or grilled mackerel near Taejongdae pier.

schedule.title: Songdo Marine Cable Car (Air Cruise) & Cloud Trails
schedule.detail: Glide across the open sea in a glass-bottom Crystal Cabin gondola between Songdo Beach and Amnam Park, then walk the curved Songdo Cloud Trails skywalk over the ocean.
schedule.logistics: Songdo Bay Station; bus or taxi from Yeongdo.

schedule.title: Huinnyeoul Culture Village Sunset
schedule.detail: Stroll the narrow coastal cliffside walkway on Yeongdo, enjoying illuminated sea tunnels and cafes with panoramic ocean views.

schedule.title: Choryang Bulgogi / Seafood Feast
schedule.detail: Savor marinated beef bulgogi or spicy octopus stir-fry (nakji bokkeum) in central Busan.

blocks.label: Dramatic Geological Wonders
blocks.text: Taejongdae and Songdo showcase Busan's most impressive coastal cliff and wave topography.

blocks.label: Ocean Gondola Experience
blocks.text: The glass-bottom cable car gives breathtaking aerial perspectives of incoming cargo ships and islands.

days.food: Lunch: Taejongdae fresh abalone porridge (jeonbok-juk). Dinner: Gaemijip spicy octopus, pork, and tripe stir-fry (Nakgobsai).

days.costNote: Songdo Cable Car Crystal Cabin ₩22,000 round-trip.
days.watchouts: Wind can be brisk on ocean cliffs; windbreaker jacket strongly recommended.
days.planB: Songdo Marine Cable Car operates in normal rain; Amnam Park indoor cafes provide shelter.

days.title: World-Class Jjimjilbang Saunas & Architectural Icons
days.anchor: Centum City Spa Land Thermal Baths → Busan Cinema Center → Shinsegae Department Store

schedule.title: Spa Land Centum City (Luxury Korean Bathhouse)
schedule.detail: Immerse in 18 natural thermal spring pools drawn from 1,000m underground, explore 13 themed aesthetic sauna rooms (Himalayan salt, Roman steam, Finnish sauna), and relax in ergonomic heated loungers.
schedule.logistics: Centum City Station Line 2 direct mall basement connection.

schedule.title: Shinsegae Centum City Gourmet Food Hall Lunch
schedule.detail: Dine in the world's largest department store food emporium, sampling gourmet Korean delicacies, artisan noodles, and dessert.

schedule.title: Busan Cinema Center (BIFF Venue)
schedule.detail: Admire the Guinness World Record cantilevered LED roof structure, home to the prestigious Busan International Film Festival, and visit cinema exhibitions.

schedule.title: Marine City Sunset Walk & The Bay 101
schedule.detail: Photograph the gleaming glass skyscraper reflections of Marine City and relax at The Bay 101 open-air deck.

schedule.title: Gourmet Korean Fried Chicken & Draft Beer (Chimaek)
schedule.detail: Celebrate with crispy golden Korean fried chicken, sweet garlic glaze, and local Busan craft beer.

blocks.label: Mid-Trip Physical Rejuvenation
blocks.text: A full 4-hour wellness soak at Spa Land relieves all accumulated travel fatigue.

blocks.label: Weather-Proof Comfort
blocks.text: All major daytime facilities are connected indoors at Centum City.

days.food: Lunch: Shinsegae Centum City Food Hall (gourmet cold noodles or Hanwoo bibimbap). Dinner: The Bay 101 fish & chips / Haeundae artisanal Korean fried chicken.

days.title: Ancient Buddhist Sanctuaries & Industrial Art Spaces
days.anchor: Beomeosa Mountain Temple → Geumjeongsanseong Fortress → F1963 Cultural Hub

schedule.title: Beomeosa Temple (Temple of the Nirvana Fish)
schedule.detail: Ascend Mount Geumjeong to tour one of Korea's premier Buddhist headquarters, founded in 678 AD, surrounded by tranquil bamboo and wisteria groves.
schedule.logistics: Beomeosa Station Line 1 Exit 5, then Bus 90 up mountain.

schedule.title: Dongnae Mountain Pajeon Lunch
schedule.detail: Savor authentic Dongnae Pajeon: thick scallion pancakes loaded with fresh squid, clams, oysters, and beef, paired with local Geumjeongsanseong Makgeolli.

schedule.title: F1963 Cultural Arts Complex & Terarosa Coffee
schedule.detail: Explore a visionary former steel wire factory transformed into an eco-friendly cultural space with Yes24 giant book store, Kukje Gallery art exhibits, and bamboo garden.
schedule.logistics: Mangmi Station Line 3 or 15-min taxi from Centum City.

schedule.title: Millak Waterfront Raw Fish Feast
schedule.detail: Enjoy sliced flounder and yellowtail sashimi overlooking the illuminated Gwangan Bridge from high-floor waterfront restaurants.

blocks.label: Mountain & Industrial Heritage
blocks.text: Contrasts a 1,300-year-old Buddhist mountain haven with 21st-century industrial art revitalization.

blocks.label: Artisanal Cuisine
blocks.text: Dongnae Pajeon is historically registered as Busan Local Intangible Cultural Asset #1.

days.food: Lunch: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon (historic scallion pancake with rice wine). Dinner: Millak Waterfront raw seasonal sashimi and spicy maeuntang.
days.reservationNote: Beomeosa Temple entry is free; open year-round.
days.costNote: Temple free; Makgeolli + Pajeon lunch ~₩20,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Bus 90 road winds up the mountain; hold handrails if standing.
days.planB: F1963 indoor exhibitions, Yes24 bookstore, and Terarosa coffee lounge are completely covered.

days.title: Peaceful Waves, Skywalks & Gentle Rhythm (CSAT / Suneung Day)

schedule.title: Igidae Coastal Cliff Walkway
schedule.detail: Walk the scenic coastal trail cut into volcanic cliff faces, offering pristine ocean views with the modern Busan skyline across the bay.

schedule.title: Oryukdo Island View Lunch

schedule.title: Oryukdo Glass Skywalk

schedule.logistics: Free admission; shoe covers provided at gate.

schedule.title: Haeundae Sunset Cafe & Rest
schedule.detail: Relax at an ocean-view cafe on Dalmaji Hill or Haeundae beachfront, reflecting on 7 wonderful Busan nights.

schedule.title: Busan Farewell Feast: Hanwoo Beef Barbecue
schedule.detail: Celebrate the final night in Busan with premium charcoal-grilled Korean Hanwoo beef tenderloin.
schedule.logistics: Haeundae Somunnan Amso Galbi-jip or premier local steakhouse.

blocks.label: CSAT Low-Stakes Alignment

blocks.label: Farewell Coastal Panorama
blocks.text: The Igidae-to-Oryukdo ridge provides one of Korea's most breathtaking coastal walking memories.

food: Lunch: Oryukdo Haemul Kalguksu (seafood noodle soup). Dinner: Haeundae Somunnan Amso Galbi (marinated beef short ribs with potato noodles).
days.reservationNote: Oryukdo Skywalk open 09:00–18:00; admission is free.
days.costNote: Skywalk is free; Final Busan Hanwoo BBQ dinner ~₩45,000–₩60,000 per person.

days.title: Capital Return: Seamless Rail Travel & Departure Buffer

schedule.title: KTX High-Speed Rail to Seoul

schedule.title: Euljiro 'Hipjiro' Lighting & Print Alleys

schedule.title: Euljiro Nogari Alley & Korean Draft Beer

days.title: Final Souvenir Curations & Celebration Feast

schedule.detail: Browse Korea's oldest traditional market for ceramics, tea accessories, dried seaweed, and handmade kitchenware, enjoying hot kalguksu.

schedule.title: Seoul Station Lotte Mart Mega-Store

blocks.label: Departure Prep
blocks.text: All shopping and packing completed by Saturday night ensures Sunday morning is 100% calm and stress-free.

blocks.label: Immediate Tax Refund

blocks.text: Direct AREX express from hotel doorstep guarantees predictable 43-minute airport transit.

blocks.label: Zero Rush
blocks.text: Arriving at 10:15 leaves ample time for customs, tax refunds, duty-free pickup, and a relaxed pre-flight meal.

days.food: Breakfast: Hotel café or airport lounge / Korean Food Street at ICN Terminal (bibimbap/soup).

itineraries.title: The Great Korean Culinary & Market Trail (Gastronomy & Street Eats)
itineraries.bestFor: Passionate food lovers, night market enthusiasts, and culinary adventurers who prioritize authentic regional flavors, Michelin bib gourmands, historic bakeries, and live seafood feasts.
itineraries.decisionSummary: An immersive gastronomic expedition linking Seoul's legendary street alleys and Hanwoo beef markets with Daejeon's beloved bakeries and noodle culture, culminating in Busan's world-famous coastal seafood emporiums.
itineraries.recommendation: Choose this route if your primary joy in travel is tasting authentic local dishes, exploring bustling night markets, and discovering centuries-old culinary traditions.
itineraries.tradeoff: Requires hearty appetite and willingness to navigate lively, bustling market alleys and try authentic fermented and spicy specialties.

schedule.detail: Sip deep roasted Ssanggwa-cha (medicinal herb tea with egg yolk) or sweet Omija tea paired with handmade yakgwa (honey pastry).

schedule.title: Ikseon-dong Dessert Alleys
schedule.detail: Sample soufflé pancakes, salt bread (so-geum bbang), and black sesame gelato in preserved hanok cafes.

schedule.title: Gwangjang Traditional Market Grand Feast
schedule.detail: Dive into the vibrant food stalls: crispy bindaetteok (mung bean pancake fried in oil), addictive mayak gimbap with mustard sauce, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare with pear and raw egg yolk).

blocks.label: Legendary Institutions
blocks.text: Pairs 60-year-old culinary stalwarts with lively street market stall culture.

blocks.label: Walkable Progression
blocks.text: Seamless walking route from Myeongdong across Cheonggyecheon to Jongno and Gwangjang.

days.food: Lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja (kalguksu & mandu). Afternoon: Traditional tea & yakgwa. Dinner: Gwangjang Market bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, yukhoe, and draft makgeolli.
days.reservationNote: Gwangjang market stalls are cash or T-Money friendly; ATM available on site.
days.costNote: Daily food budget ~₩45,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Yukhoe alley can have brief lines during evening peak; stall rotation is fast.
days.planB: Gwangjang covered market roof shields from any autumn rain.

days.title: Local Market Stalls, Pajeon Skewers & Charcoal Ribs
days.anchor: Mangwon Neighborhood Food Market → Yeonnam Micro-Bakeries → Mapo Charcoal Galbi & Gongdeok Jeon Alley

schedule.title: Mangwon Traditional Market Exploration
schedule.detail: Sample beloved local snacks: sweet & spicy boneless fried chicken (dakgangjeong), marshmallow ice cream, and handmade croquettes.

schedule.title: Yeonnam-dong Artisan Coffee & Salt Bread
schedule.detail: Stroll Gyeongui Line Forest Park and discover Seoul's finest specialty third-wave coffee roasters and French butter salt bread bakeries.

schedule.title: Gongdeok Jeon (Pancake) & Jokbal Alley
schedule.detail: Pick your own assortment of freshly fried savory pancakes (jeon, stuffed peppers, shrimp, fish) piled onto wicker trays.

schedule.title: Mapo Charcoal Pork Galbi Feast
schedule.detail: Feast on succulent pork ribs marinated in sweet soy and garlic, grilled over glowing hardwood charcoal with steaming egg custard.

blocks.label: Authentic Local Markets
blocks.text: Mangwon is beloved by Seoul locals for authentic neighborhood pricing and artisan snack variety.

blocks.label: Mapo Meat Heritage
blocks.text: Mapo is the historic birthplace of Seoul's charcoal galbi restaurant culture.

days.food: Lunch: Mangwon Market street snacks (dakgangjeong & croquettes). Afternoon: Gongdeok assorted savory pancakes (jeon). Dinner: Mapo charcoal-grilled pork galbi with cold dongchimi noodles.
days.reservationNote: Gongdeok Jeon alley is self-serve selection; pay by weight at the register.
days.costNote: Daily food budget ~₩48,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Gongdeok gets lively with local office workers around 18:00; visit early.
days.planB: Mangwon Market is a fully covered arcade; Gongdeok restaurants are indoor.

days.title: Korea's Crown Jewel Beef & Modernist Coffee Alleys
days.anchor: Majang Meat Market 1++ Hanwoo Beef Tasting → Seongsu Industrial Lofts & Bakeries

schedule.title: Majang Meat Market & Hanwoo Barbecue
schedule.detail: Browse Korea's premier meat wholesale district; select prime 1++ Korean Hanwoo beef ribeye, sirloin, and chuck flap, grilling it immediately at a second-floor charcoal restaurant.
schedule.logistics: Majang Station Line 5 Exit 2 or Yongdu Station Line 2.

schedule.title: Seongsu-dong Cafe Hub (Center Coffee, Daelim Warehouse)
schedule.detail: Explore converted industrial shoe factories housing world-class barista counters, pour-over specialty brews, and bakery showrooms.

schedule.title: Seoul Forest Autumn Walk & Digestive Break
schedule.detail: Walk under golden ginkgo trees in Seoul Forest to refresh between heavy feasts.
schedule.logistics: Seoul Forest Station Suin-Bundang Line Exit 4.

schedule.title: Seongsu Modern Korean Pub (Jumak)
schedule.detail: Pair regional cloudy rice wines (craft makgeolli) with crispy potato pancakes and braised pork belly.

blocks.label: Crown Jewel Beef
blocks.text: 1++ Hanwoo is Korea's celebrated indigenous marbling standard, unmatched in tenderness and flavor.

blocks.label: Artisan Contrast
blocks.text: Balances raw butcher market traditions with ultra-chic Seongsu coffee culture.

days.food: Lunch: Majang Market 1++ Hanwoo beef charcoal grill with doenjang jjigae. Afternoon: Seongsu artisanal pour-over coffee & canelé. Dinner: Seongsu craft makgeolli & crispy gamjajeon potato pancake.
days.reservationNote: In Majang Market, purchase meat cuts on 1F butcher counters, then pay small table-setting fee (₩6,000) at 2F grill restaurant.
days.costNote: Hanwoo lunch ~₩60,000–₩85,000 per person; exceptional value compared to hotel steakhouses.
days.watchouts: Hanwoo is rich; enjoy with ssam leafy greens and wasabi.
days.planB: Majang indoor dining rooms and Seongsu cavernous cafes are warm and weather-proof.

days.title: Ocean Bounty in the Capital & Legendary Simmering Rice Cakes
days.anchor: Noryangjin Fish Market Seafood Auction & Sashimi → Sindang-dong Tteokbokki Town

schedule.title: Noryangjin Wholesale Fisheries Market
schedule.detail: Explore the massive multi-level fish market, selecting live king crab, snow crab, or fresh seasonal flatfish sashimi prepared fresh on the spot with spicy fish stew (maeuntang).
schedule.logistics: Noryangjin Station Line 1/9 direct footbridge connection.

schedule.title: Yeouido The Hyundai Gourmet Supermarket
schedule.detail: Browse the sprawling Tasty Seoul basement food hall, discovering boutique confectioneries, matcha lattes, and artisan snacks.
schedule.logistics: Yeouido Station Line 5/9 or Yeouinaru Station.

schedule.title: Cheonggyecheon Stream Evening Stroll
schedule.detail: Stroll illuminated urban waterfalls to work up an appetite.

schedule.title: Sindang-dong Tteokbokki Town Feasting
schedule.detail: Experience the historic 1953 birthplace of instant tteokbokki (Mabongnim Halmeoni), boiling rice cakes, fish cakes, ramen noodles, fried dumplings, and sweet black bean chili paste at the table.

blocks.label: Seafood to Street Food
blocks.text: Transitions from high-end marine treasures at Noryangjin to cozy, nostalgic street comfort food in Sindang.

blocks.label: Historic Pedigree
blocks.text: Mabongnim Halmeoni restaurant has perfected tabletop tteokbokki for over 70 years.

days.food: Lunch: Noryangjin fresh sashimi, butter-grilled abalone, and spicy maeuntang. Dinner: Sindang-dong Mabongnim Tteokbokki bubbling hot pot with fried dumplings and cheese.
days.reservationNote: Noryangjin restaurant charges cooking fee (₩5,000–₩10,000 per kg) for steaming crab or grilling.
days.costNote: Noryangjin lunch ~₩45,000 per person; Tteokbokki dinner ~₩12,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Fish market floors can be damp; wear closed-toe walking shoes.
days.planB: Noryangjin modern building and The Hyundai Seoul are completely enclosed and climate-controlled.

days.title: Smoky Briquette Grills & Industrial Alleys
days.anchor: Dongdaemun Grilled Fish Street → DDP Night Architecture → Euljiro Nogari Draft Beer Alley

schedule.title: Dongdaemun Grilled Fish Alley (Saengseon Gui)
schedule.detail: Dine in a narrow alley where fresh mackerel, Spanish mackerel (samchi), and croaker are continuously grilled over smoky outdoor briquettes until skin is blistered and crispy.

schedule.title: Dongdaemun Design Plaza & Fashion Arcade
schedule.detail: Explore DDP design exhibitions and surrounding textile fabric markets.

schedule.title: Central Seoul Gourmet Dessert Cafe Stroll
schedule.detail: Enjoy Korean shaved ice dessert (bingsu) topped with sweet red beans, injeolmi rice cakes, and roasted soybean powder.

schedule.title: Euljiro 'Hipjiro' Nogari Alley & Grilled Pork
schedule.detail: Join thousands of locals enjoying fresh draft lager, grilled dried pollack (nogari), garlic chicken, and thick pork collar in retro industrial alleys.

blocks.label: Everyday Culinary Soul
blocks.text: Showcases the comforting, unpretentious alley dishes that fuel Seoul's working culture.

blocks.label: Retro Atmosphere
blocks.text: Euljiro outdoor seating under glowing paper lanterns is an unforgettable cultural experience.

days.food: Lunch: Dongdaemun briquette-grilled mackerel and spicy stir-fried squid (ojingeo bokkeum). Afternoon: Injeolmi Sulbing shaved ice. Dinner: Euljiro Nogari Alley draft beer, garlic chicken, and grilled pollack.
days.reservationNote: Fish alley restaurants serve unlimited side dishes and warm rice with fish sets.
days.costNote: Fish lunch ~₩12,000; Sulbing ~₩7,000; Euljiro beer night ~₩20,000.
days.watchouts: Dress warmly for Euljiro outdoor tables in November evening breezes.
days.planB: Indoor seating available in all Euljiro pubs if chilly.

days.title: Slow-Simmered Comfort & Weekend Market Prep
days.anchor: Hadongkwan 80-Year Gomtang Beef Soup → Samcheongdong Sujebi → Sunday Train Prep

schedule.title: Hadongkwan Traditional Beef Gomtang
schedule.detail: Taste Seoul's definitive slow-simmered beef brisket soup (founded in 1939), served with tender tripe, spring onions, and aged radish kkakdugi.

schedule.title: Samcheong-dong Sujebi & Bukchon Walk
schedule.detail: Enjoy hand-torn dough pasta cooked in rich anchovy broth with tender clams in an earthenware pot.

schedule.title: Seoul Station Lotte Mart Food Reconnaissance
schedule.detail: Preview Korean food gifts and pick up snacks for tomorrow morning KTX journey to Daejeon.

schedule.title: Feast of Chuncheon Dakgalbi (Spicy Stir-Fried Chicken)
schedule.detail: Savor spicy gochujang-marinated chicken, cabbage, sweet potatoes, and chewy rice cakes cooked on a giant tabletop cast iron skillet, finished with fried rice.

blocks.label: Restorative Broths
blocks.text: Hadongkwan and Samcheongdong Sujebi highlight Korea's mastery of comforting bone and anchovy broths.

blocks.label: Transit Preparation
blocks.text: Packing early ensures a seamless Sunday morning KTX departure to Daejeon.

days.food: Breakfast/Brunch: Hadongkwan traditional Hanwoo gomtang soup. Lunch: Samcheong-dong handmade sujebi and gamjajeon. Dinner: Chuncheon spicy dakgalbi with mozzarella cheese and bokkeumbap.
days.reservationNote: Hadongkwan closes early when broth runs out (typically around 15:30); go for morning brunch.
days.costNote: Daily food budget ~₩40,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Dakgalbi sauce can splatter; wear the provided restaurant aprons.
days.planB: All dining venues are fully enclosed indoors.

days.title: Korea's Bread Capital & Signature Fiery Tofu
days.anchor: Morning KTX to Daejeon → Sung Sim Dang Bakery Mega-Trail → Daeheung-dong Spicy Tofu

schedule.title: KTX High-Speed Rail Seoul to Daejeon
schedule.detail: 55-minute smooth train transit from Seoul Station to Daejeon Station.

schedule.title: Sung Sim Dang Legendary Bakery (Main Branch & Cake Boutique)
schedule.detail: Explore the multi-floor bakery empire: fresh Twigim Soboro (fried streusel pastry filled with sweet red bean), Bochoo Bread (leek & egg bun), and pure cream cakes.

schedule.title: Hotel Check-in & Rest in Yuseong / Dunsan
schedule.detail: Check into Daejeon hotel and drop luggage.
schedule.logistics: Metro Line 1 to Yuseong Spa Station.

schedule.title: Jungang Market Street Snack Crawl
schedule.detail: Sample Daejeon traditional market specialties: handmade perilla oil seaweed, sundae blood sausage, and hot sugar-filled hotteok.
schedule.logistics: Daejeon Jungang Market adjacent to station.

schedule.title: Daeheung-dong Gwangcheon Sikdang Dubu Duruchigi
schedule.detail: Feast on Daejeon legendary local dish: thick braised tofu cubes simmered in fiery red pepper broth, tossed with boiled kalguksu noodles.

blocks.label: Bakery Capital of Korea
blocks.text: Sung Sim Dang is a national cultural icon, drawing pastry lovers from across the country.

blocks.label: Daejeon Soul Food
blocks.text: Dubu Duruchigi is Daejeon's unique spicy comfort food invention.

days.food: Lunch: Sung Sim Dang fresh warm pastries and Cake Boutique tarts. Dinner: Gwangcheon Sikdang spicy Dubu Duruchigi (braised tofu stir-fry with noodles and boiled pork suyuk).
days.reservationNote: Book KTX train 30 days prior on Korail app.
days.costNote: KTX fare ~₩23,700; Sung Sim Dang pastries ~₩15,000; Dinner ~₩18,000.
days.watchouts: Dubu Duruchigi is genuinely spicy; ask for mild ('deol-maep-ge') if sensitive.
days.planB: Sung Sim Dang and Gwangcheon Sikdang are comfortable indoor venues.

days.title: Hand-Cut Noodle Heritage & Open-Air Market Aromas
days.anchor: Daejeon Kalguksu Alley Pilgrimage → Yuseong Traditional 5-Day Market

schedule.title: Daejeon Hand-Cut Kalguksu Pilgrimage (Smoky Clam & Spicy Perilla)
schedule.detail: Taste Daejeon famous spicy clam kalguksu (Eolkeuni Kalguksu) enriched with crown daisy (ssukgat) and beaten egg.

schedule.title: Yuseong Traditional 5-Day Market & Street Treats
schedule.detail: Browse lively outdoor stalls selling roasted sweet chestnuts, fresh steamed corn, crispy hot bindaetteok, and traditional herbal medicines.
schedule.logistics: Yuseong Market area (held on dates ending in 4 and 9).

schedule.title: Yuseong Outdoor Foot Bath Spring Reset
schedule.detail: Soak feet in 42°C natural hot spring mineral waters while sipping roasted iced barley tea.

schedule.title: Daejeon Suyuk & Bossam Dinner
schedule.detail: Enjoy tender boiled pork belly wrapped in freshly salted kimchi and sweet garlic sauce.

blocks.label: Noodle Capital Heritage
blocks.text: Daejeon developed Korea's most diverse kalguksu culture due to historic railway grain depots.

blocks.label: Market Authenticity
blocks.text: Yuseong 5-day market offers unfiltered regional market sights, sounds, and snacks.

days.food: Lunch: Famous Eolkeuni spicy clam kalguksu with ssukgat herbs. Dinner: Yuseong tender pork bossam with fresh oyster kimchi.
days.reservationNote: Yuseong Market occurs on 4th, 9th, 14th, 19th, 24th, 29th of each month (Nov 9 is a market day!).
days.costNote: Noodles ~₩9,000; Market snacks ~₩8,000; Bossam dinner ~₩25,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Foot bath requires removing shoes; clean feet at washing tap before entering pool.
days.planB: Indoor restaurants throughout Yuseong Spa district provide sheltered dining.

days.title: Ancient Woodland Recipes & Sky-High Gourmet Delights
days.anchor: Gujeuk Muk-maeul (Acorn Jelly Village) → Shinsegae Art & Science Gourmet Hub

schedule.title: Gujeuk Muk-maeul (Historic Acorn Jelly Village)
schedule.detail: Visit Daejeon dedicated acorn jelly heritage village for warm Chae-muk (shredded acorn jelly in savory dried anchovy & kimchi broth) and acorn flour pancakes.

schedule.title: Expo Science Park & Hanbit Promenade Walk
schedule.detail: Digestive stroll around Hanbit Tower and Gapcheon River pedestrian bridge.

schedule.title: Shinsegae Art & Science Gourmet Market & Sky Lounge
schedule.detail: Explore the 38th-floor panoramic sky cafe and sample premium artisanal Korean pastries and boutique gelato.

schedule.title: Daejeon Stone-Pot Bulgogi Feast
schedule.detail: Savor thinly sliced marinated Korean beef simmered in sweet soy broth with glass noodles and enoki mushrooms in a piping hot earthenware bowl.

blocks.label: Unique Regional Specialty
blocks.text: Acorn jelly soup (dotorimuk-bap) is a historic Daejeon folk culinary treasure.

blocks.label: Elevated Panoramas
blocks.text: Shinsegae 38F lounge provides 360-degree sunset views over Daejeon valley.

days.food: Lunch: Gujeuk village warm Chae-muk acorn jelly soup with acorn pancake (muk-jeon). Dinner: Dunsan sizzling stone-pot beef bulgogi with seasonal banchan.
days.reservationNote: Gujeuk muk-maeul restaurants are open daily 10:00–20:00.
days.costNote: Muk lunch ~₩11,000; Sky lounge coffee ~₩6,500; Dinner ~₩22,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Acorn jelly has a subtle, pleasant herbal bitterness; season with kimchi and seaweed flakes.
days.planB: Shinsegae Art & Science is a multi-floor weatherproof indoor paradise.

days.title: Country Mountain Greens & Rich Herbal Duck Stew
days.anchor: Gyejoksan Forest Walk → Yuseong Perilla Duck Stew (Oritang) Banquet

schedule.title: Gyejoksan Mountain Autumn Trail Walk
schedule.detail: Take an invigorating autumn hike through pine woods to Gyejoksanseong fortress.
schedule.logistics: City Bus 74 or taxi to trail entrance.

schedule.title: Country Village Dotorimuk & Potato Pancake
schedule.detail: Refuel with freshly made potato pancakes and seasoned mountain greens at a trailhead rustic lodge.

schedule.title: Yuseong Thermal Spa Bathhouse Soak
schedule.detail: Full mineral hot spring bath to soothe legs and stimulate appetite.

schedule.title: Yuseong Famous Perilla Duck Stew (Oritang)
schedule.detail: Feast on rich, creamy simmered duck stew loaded with toasted perilla powder, water dropwort (minari), and wild mountain leeks.
schedule.logistics: Yuseong Hot Springs duck stew street.

blocks.label: Nutritional Stamina
blocks.text: Korean duck stew (Oritang) with perilla seed is considered the pinnacle of autumn stamina cuisine (boyang-sik).

blocks.label: Mountain to Mineral Spa
blocks.text: Pairs active morning hill walking with deeply relaxing evening hot spring bathing.

days.food: Lunch: Rustic potato pancake and wild mountain herb bibimbap. Dinner: Yuseong bubbling Oritang duck stew with toasted perilla seeds and minari greens.
days.reservationNote: Hot spring bathhouse fee ~₩10,000 payable at door.
days.costNote: Lunch ~₩14,000; Hot spring ~₩10,000; Duck stew feast ~₩30,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Duck stew is served boiling hot in earthenware; dip tender duck meat in cho-gochujang perilla sauce.
days.planB: Yuseong spa facilities and duck stew dining halls are warm and sheltered.

days.title: Futuristic Bakery Showrooms & High-Stamina Feasts
days.anchor: Sung Sim Dang DCC Robotic Bakery → Charcoal-Grilled Freshwater Eel Feast

schedule.title: Sung Sim Dang DCC Branch & Bakery Lab
schedule.detail: Witness robotic tray delivery, sample freshly pulled sourdough, butter brioches, and signature walnut pies.

schedule.title: Hanbat Arboretum Autumn Stroll
schedule.detail: Gentle walk among golden metasequoias and outdoor sculpture gardens.

schedule.title: Dunsan Cafe Boulevard Artisanal Dessert
schedule.detail: Taste Korean bingsu or specialty hand-drip coffees.

schedule.title: Daejeon Charcoal-Grilled Freshwater Eel (Jangeo-gui)
schedule.detail: Savor thick cuts of freshwater eel grilled table-side over charcoal with sweet teriyaki ginger glaze and pickled ginger slivers.

blocks.label: Bakery Innovation
blocks.text: DCC branch showcases high-tech modern iterations of Sung Sim Dang's master baking.

blocks.label: Eel Stamina Banquet
blocks.text: Freshwater eel provides rich omega-3 nutrients and rich flavor to prepare for coastal Busan.

days.food: Lunch: Sung Sim Dang DCC bakery brunch and freshly pressed fruit juices. Dinner: Table-side charcoal-grilled freshwater eel with seasoned sticky rice.
days.reservationNote: No reservations needed for DCC bakery; peak hours 12:00–14:00.
days.costNote: Bakery lunch ~₩15,000; Charcoal eel banquet ~₩38,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Wrap grilled eel with fresh perilla leaf, sliced garlic, and ginger to balance richness.
days.planB: DCC complex and eel restaurants are spacious and indoors.

days.title: Maritime Arrival, Wheat Noodle Legends & Coastal Street Feasts
days.anchor: KTX Daejeon to Busan (1h30m) → Choryang Milmyeon → Haeundae Market Grilled Clams & Sea Eel

schedule.title: KTX High-Speed Rail to Busan
schedule.detail: Scenic 90-minute rail journey arriving at Busan Station on the southern sea.

schedule.title: Choryang Milmyeon (Busan Wheat Noodle Icon)
schedule.detail: Taste authentic Busan Milmyeon: cold wheat noodles in chilled spiced broth with cucumber, boiled beef, and hot kettle broth.

schedule.title: Metro to Haeundae Beach Base & Check-in
schedule.detail: Check into Haeundae hotel (e.g. L7 Haeundae or Felix by STX).
schedule.logistics: Metro Line 2 or taxi along harbor bridge.

schedule.title: Haeundae Beach Promenade Walk
schedule.detail: Breathe fresh sea air walking from Dongbaek Island to Haeundae beach.

schedule.title: Haeundae Traditional Market Feast
schedule.detail: Sample sizzling grilled sea eel (godeulbaegi), fresh seafood hot pot, Korean tteokbokki, and famous Busan ssiat hotteok (brown sugar seed pancake).

blocks.label: Iconic Busan Wheat Noodles
blocks.text: Milmyeon is Busan's historical Korean War innovation, substituting wheat flour for buckwheat.

blocks.label: Night Market Vibrancy
blocks.text: Haeundae Market comes alive at night with smoking street stalls and live seafood tanks.

days.food: Lunch: Choryang Milmyeon (cold wheat noodles & giant steamed mandu). Dinner: Haeundae Market grilled sea eel, seafood pajeon, and ssiat hotteok.
days.reservationNote: Book KTX Daejeon→Busan on Korail app 30 days prior.
days.costNote: KTX ticket ~₩36,200; Milmyeon ~₩8,500; Market dinner ~₩25,000.
days.watchouts: Sea eel is grilled with spicy red pepper sauce; ask for non-spicy salt grill (sogeum-gui) if preferred.
days.planB: Haeundae market is a covered pedestrian street.

days.title: Ocean Clam Grills, Live Sashimi & Saturday Drones
days.anchor: Cheongsapo Seaside Grilled Clams (Jogae-gui) → Millak Raw Fish Town & Gwangan Drone Show

schedule.title: Cheongsapo Fishing Village & Grilled Clam Feast
schedule.detail: Dine in an oceanfront terrace enjoying a giant platter of live scallops, clams, and abalone grilled over briquettes with butter, cheese, and spicy dipping sauce.
schedule.logistics: Blueline Park Sky Capsule or short taxi to Cheongsapo.

schedule.title: Cheongsapo Cafe Street & Ocean Skywalk
schedule.detail: Sip artisanal pour-over coffee overlooking the red & white lighthouses and walk Daritdol Skywalk over the waves.

schedule.title: Gwangalli Beach Sunset Walk
schedule.detail: Watch the sun dip behind Gwangan Suspension Bridge from the sandy beachfront.

schedule.title: Millak Raw Fish Town & Saturday Night Drone Show
schedule.detail: Feast on seasonal sliced yellowtail (bangeo) and flounder sashimi with sea views, stepping out onto the sand to watch 500+ synchronized LED drones dance in the night sky.
schedule.logistics: Millak Raw Fish Tower / Gwangalli Beach (drones at 19:00 & 21:00).

blocks.label: Oceanfront Charcoal Grilling
blocks.text: Cheongsapo's clam grilling tradition combines crashing waves with buttery charcoal-cooked shellfish.

blocks.label: Saturday Night Highlight
blocks.text: Gwangalli drone performance over Gwangan Diamond Bridge is Busan's premier evening spectacle.

days.food: Lunch: Cheongsapo seaside grilled live clams (jogae-gui) with butter and melted cheese. Dinner: Millak Raw Fish Town sliced yellowtail sashimi, abalone, and spicy fish stew.
days.reservationNote: Book Sky Capsule 14 days in advance on official website.
days.costNote: Clam feast ~₩35,000 per person; Sashimi banquet ~₩40,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Clam shells get hot on the grill; use provided cloth gloves and tongs.
days.planB: Millak raw fish buildings have panoramic glass indoor dining rooms.

days.title: Korea's Marine Epicenter & Vibrant Night Street Eats
days.anchor: Jagalchi Fish Market Giant Seafood Feast → Bupyeong Kkangtong Night Market

schedule.title: Jagalchi Fish Market Giant Seafood Banquet
schedule.detail: Pick live King Crab, Snow Crab, or live octopus (san-nakji) from 1F stalls and have it steamed and prepared immediately on 2F with crab-roe fried rice.

schedule.title: BIFF Square Snack Crawl
schedule.detail: Taste original seed hotteok (crispy brown sugar pancake filled with sunflower seeds and pine nuts) and spicy rice cake skewers.

schedule.title: Gamcheon Culture Village Sunset Walk
schedule.detail: Stroll colorful hillside alleys and photograph the pastel harbor vistas.

schedule.title: Bupyeong Kkangtong Night Market Feasting
schedule.detail: Sample iconic night market street dishes: Bibim Dangmyeon (glass noodles with spicy seasoning), giant fried Busan fishcakes (Eomuk), skewered grilled pork, and rolled egg omelets.

blocks.label: Seafood Epicenter
blocks.text: Jagalchi is the largest and most legendary marine market in East Asia.

blocks.label: Street Food Variety
blocks.text: Bupyeong Kkangtong is Korea's first official permanent night street food market.

days.food: Lunch: Jagalchi Market steamed giant king crab with fried rice in crab carapace and seafood stew. Dinner: Bupyeong Kkangtong Night Market bibim dangmyeon, Samjin fishcakes, and street snacks.
days.reservationNote: Market stalls are cash / T-Money preferred; cards accepted in 2F restaurants.
days.costNote: King Crab lunch ~₩55,000–₩75,000 per person; Night market ~₩18,000.
days.watchouts: Crab prices are seasonal by weight; negotiate price before cooking.
days.planB: Jagalchi building and Bupyeong market are covered arcade facilities.

days.title: Steamed Coastal Snow Crabs & Oceanic Porridge Cauldron
days.anchor: Gijang Snow Crab Market → Yeonhwa-ri Abalone Porridge Village

schedule.title: Gijang Market Live Snow Crab Feast
schedule.detail: Select live Russian snow crabs and red king crabs from steaming wooden cedar boxes in Gijang market, served with rich crab-butter fried rice.
schedule.logistics: Donghae Line to Gijang Station or 25-min taxi from Haeundae.

schedule.title: Yeonhwa-ri Coastal Tent Village & Sea-View Cafe
schedule.detail: Stroll past the scenic orange and red lighthouses and enjoy coffee at a modern oceanfront cafe in Gijang.

schedule.title: Ananti Cove Ocean Promenade
schedule.detail: Relax along the coastal cliffs of Osiria tourism complex.

schedule.title: Yeonhwa-ri Abalone Porridge (Jeonbok-juk) Cauldron
schedule.detail: Dine on thick, emerald-green abalone porridge simmered with whole abalone entrails and sesame oil in a massive cast iron pot.

blocks.label: Gijang Snow Crab Authority
blocks.text: Gijang is Korea's premier East Sea snow crab distribution hub, offering peak freshness and direct wholesale value.

blocks.label: Abalone Intestine Porridge
blocks.text: True Busan jeonbok-juk is emerald green from the fresh abalone liver (geu), imparting deep oceanic umami.

days.food: Lunch: Gijang Market freshly steamed snow crab with seasoned crab-roe rice. Dinner: Yeonhwa-ri traditional abalone porridge (jeonbok-juk) in a cast iron pot.
days.reservationNote: Gijang market vendors offer steaming service included with crab purchase.
days.costNote: Snow crab lunch ~₩50,000–₩70,000 per person; Abalone porridge ~₩15,000 per person.
days.watchouts: Abalone porridge is cooked fresh to order in cauldrons; allow 20 mins preparation time.
days.planB: Gijang crab restaurants and Ananti complexes are comfortable and indoor.

days.title: Royal Scallion Pancakes & Mountain Artisanal Rice Wine
days.anchor: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon (80-Year Lineage) → Geumjeongsanseong Makgeolli Brewery Tasting

schedule.title: Beomeosa Mountain Temple Autumn Walk
schedule.detail: Scenic mountain stroll to work up an appetite.

schedule.title: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon (Busan Cultural Asset #1)
schedule.detail: Feast on Korea's most celebrated scallion pancake: tender young green onions layered with beef, squid, mussels, and oysters in a glutinous rice batter, steamed with beaten egg.

schedule.title: Geumjeongsanseong Mountain Village & Makgeolli Tasting
schedule.detail: Sample Korea's only designated Food Master Makgeolli #1, crafted using traditional 500-year-old wheat nuruk fermentation in mountain stone rooms.
schedule.logistics: Sanseong village; Bus 203 from Oncheonjang Station.

schedule.title: Oncheonjang Natural Hot Spring Foot Bath
schedule.detail: Rest tired feet in historic Oncheonjang outdoor mineral hot springs.

schedule.title: Korean Fried Chicken & Busan Craft Draft
schedule.detail: Crispy golden fried chicken in Haeundae.

blocks.label: Intangible Cultural Asset
blocks.text: Dongnae Pajeon was historically presented to Joseon kings and is distinct from ordinary flat jeon.

blocks.label: Designated Folk Wine
blocks.text: Geumjeongsanseong Makgeolli is Korea's most historic artisanal rice wine.

days.food: Lunch: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon (royal scallion seafood pancake) paired with Geumjeongsanseong Makgeolli. Dinner: Haeundae gourmet fried chicken with honey garlic sauce.

days.costNote: Dongnae Pajeon lunch ~₩25,000 per person; Makgeolli ~₩5,000 bottle.

days.planB: Dongnae Pajeon restaurant and Oncheonjang spa are fully indoor.

days.title: Boiling Pork Bone Cauldrons & Atmospheric Orange Tents
days.anchor: Songjeong 3-dae Dwaeji Gukbap Alley → Seomyeon Pojangmacha Street Tents

schedule.title: Songjeong 3-dae Gukbap (Since 1946)
schedule.detail: Savor authentic Busan Dwaeji Gukbap: 24-hour simmered milky pork bone broth loaded with tender pork shoulder, spicy seasoned chives (buchu), and fermented saeujeot shrimp.

schedule.title: Seomyeon Youth Street & Cafe Alleys (Jeonpo-dong)
schedule.detail: Explore transformed tool-workshop cafes, artisan dessert bakeries, and specialty matcha shops in Jeonpo.

schedule.title: Centum City Spa Land Thermal Soak

schedule.title: Seomyeon Pojangmacha (Orange Street Tents) Night

schedule.logistics: Lotte Department Store Seomyeon back alley.

blocks.label: 70-Year Soup Lineage

days.food: Lunch: Songjeong 3-dae Dwaeji Gukbap (pork soup with suyuk boiled pork). Afternoon: Jeonpo artisan pastry & coffee. Dinner: Seomyeon Pojangmacha street tents (grilled spam, eggs, spicy octopus, and soju).

days.planB: Seomyeon underground shopping mall and Gukbap restaurants are completely indoor.

schedule.title: Dalmaji Hill Scenic Coastal Walk
schedule.detail: Gentle stroll along pine-covered Dalmaji Hill overlooking the sparkling Korea Strait.
schedule.logistics: Walk from Haeundae or short taxi.

schedule.title: Cheongsapo Seafood Stew & Grilled Fish Lunch

schedule.title: Traditional Korean Tea & Rice Cake Atelier

schedule.title: Busan Farewell Feast: Hanwoo Beef Short Ribs

blocks.label: Epicurean Finale

itineraries.title: Joseon Dynasty, Hanok Living & Fine Arts (Heritage & Aesthetics)
itineraries.bestFor: History enthusiasts, art lovers, architects, and travelers who appreciate UNESCO World Heritage palaces, serene Buddhist temple architecture, modernist galleries, and classical Confucian gardens.
itineraries.decisionSummary: A contemplative, culturally rich route focusing on imperial Joseon palaces, the sublime Room of Quiet Contemplation, Daejeon's Lee Ungno modernist museum, and Busan's 1,300-year-old mountain temples and post-industrial art hubs.
itineraries.recommendation: Choose this route if you want to explore the deepest layers of Korea's 5,000-year artistic and architectural legacy with unhurried, aesthetic pacing.
itineraries.tradeoff: More time devoted to museums, traditional craft workshops, and temple contemplation rather than high-intensity nightlife or theme parks.

bases.why: Central subway interchange (Line 1/4/2 access), direct AREX connection, easy walking to Deoksugung, Namdaemun, and Myeongdong, and minimal friction for the Sunday morning KTX departure.

Nine Tree Premier Hotel Myeongdong II

bases.why: Direct subway connection (Line 1) to Daejeon KTX Station, natural mineral hot spring foot baths on the street, and close proximity to KAIST, Expo Science Park, and Hanbat Arboretum.
hotelIdeas: Yuseong Hotel / Ramada by Wyndham Daejeon

bases.why: Walk to Haeundae Beach, Blueline Park coastal train, Centum City Spa Land, and direct bus/metro connections across the eastern and southern coast.

transfers.recommended: KTX High-Speed Rail (approx. 1 hour 30 minutes, direct).
transfers.why: Fastest and most comfortable connection from central Daejeon to coastal Busan, arriving in time for check-in and sunset seafood dinner.

transfers.recommended: KTX High-Speed Rail (approx. 2 hours 15 minutes, direct).
